headline: Steel Ministry asks SAIL and NMDC to acquire overseas mineral assets
hook: Securing raw materials to tame input costs
summary: The Steel Ministry has directed state-run SAIL and NMDC to explore overseas mineral assets to secure long-term supplies and reduce input costs. India currently imports 85-90% of its coking coal needs from countries like Australia and Mozambique. The move mirrors private sector strategies, such as JSW Steel acquiring captive coking coal assets. NMDC is also diversifying to earn 20% of its revenue from non-iron ore minerals by 2030. For retail investors, captive asset acquisition could help state-run steelmakers hedge against volatile global raw material prices.
why_it_matters: State steelmakers target foreign mines to hedge raw material price volatility
winners_losers: SAIL and NMDC gain / raw material suppliers hurt
